question: Pipe P can fill (2)/(3) part of a tank in 24 hours, and pipe Q can fill (2)/(3) part of the same tank in 16 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 4 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 5 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Time for P to fill tank = 24 × (3/2) = 36 hr. Q = 16 × (3/2) = 24 hr. Total capacity = LCM(36, 24) = 72 units.

Efficiency of P = +2, Q = +3. Water filled in 4 hr = 4 × (2 + 3) = 20 units.

R empties 20 units in 5 hr, so efficiency of R = −20 ÷ 5 = −4.

Combined efficiency of (P + Q + R) = 2 + 3 − 4 = +1.

Time taken to fill the tank together = 72 ÷ 1 = 72 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 72 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe P fills 2/3 of the tank in 24 hours.

Pipe Q fills 2/3 of the tank in 16 hours.

Both P and Q were kept open for 4 hours, and then pipe R emptied the filled water in 5 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

**Calculation:**

⇒ Time taken by P to fill the full tank = 24 × (3/2) = 36 hours

⇒ Time taken by Q to fill the full tank = 16 × (3/2) = 24 hours

⇒ Water filled by P and Q in 4 hours = 4 × (2 + 3) = 20 units

⇒ Pipe R empties these 20 units in 5 hours.

⇒ Efficiency of pipe R = −20 ÷ 5 = −4 units/hr (Negative sign indicates emptying)

⇒ Combined efficiency of pipes P, Q, and R together = 2 + 3 − 4 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Time required for P, Q, and R to fill the tank = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 72 ÷ 1 = 72 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 72 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

Inlet pipes add water to the tank and are assigned a positive efficiency. Outlet pipes remove water and are assigned a negative efficiency.

LCM Method for Total Capacity

The total capacity of a tank is assumed to be the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the times taken by individual pipes to fill or empty it.

Combined Work Rule

When multiple pipes operate together, their effective efficiency is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies. Total time = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency.
